## Vacanță la mare în Bulgaria 2026: Sunny Beach, Sozopol, Nessebar — ghid complet cu prețuri

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/cazari/vacanta-bulgaria-2026-ghid-complet
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** cazari
**Publicat:** 2026-07-13
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-13

**Descriere:** Ghid complet pentru vacanță în Bulgaria 2026. Sunny Beach, Sozopol, Nessebar, Nisipurile de Aur — zone, prețuri all-inclusive, cum ajungi, ce vizitezi și sfaturi practice.

**Rezumat rapid:** Un sejur all-inclusive de 7 nopți pe litoralul bulgăresc pornește de la 250 EUR/persoană la hotel 3★ cu autocar, sau de la 350 EUR cu zbor charter. Bulgaria a adoptat euro în 2026, deci nu mai e nevoie de schimb valutar. Cu intrarea României în Schengen, cozile la vamă au dispărut. Sunny Beach e cea mai mare stațiune (8 km de plajă), Sozopol e cea mai frumoasă, iar Nessebar (UNESCO) e la 5 minute de Sunny Beach — combini plajă cu istorie.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Cât costă o vacanță all-inclusive în Bulgaria în 2026?**
R: Un sejur de 7 nopți all-inclusive pornește de la 250 EUR/persoană cu autocar (hotel 3★) și de la 350-500 EUR cu zbor charter (hotel 4★). Early booking (rezervare înainte de martie) aduce reduceri de 20-30%. Prețurile sunt cu 30-50% mai mici decât echivalentele din Turcia sau Grecia.

**Î: Bulgaria sau Turcia — care e mai bună?**
R: Bulgaria câștigă pe: proximitate (5 ore cu mașina vs. 2 ore zbor), preț (cu 20-30% mai ieftin), și NU ai nevoie de pașaport (ajunge buletinul). Turcia câștigă pe: calitatea hotelurilor (mai noi și mai mari), vreme mai sigură, și diversitate gastronomică. Pentru familii cu copii mici, Bulgaria e mai practică; pentru cupluri care vor lux, Turcia e mai bună.

**Î: Am nevoie de pașaport pentru Bulgaria?**
R: Nu. Bulgaria e în UE și, din 2025, în Schengen. Buletinul românesc e suficient. Nu mai sunt cozi la vamă — treci granița ca pe un drum intern. Euro e moneda oficială din ianuarie 2026.

**Î: Cum ajung pe litoralul bulgăresc?**
R: Cu mașina: București → Sunny Beach: 5 ore (prin Giurgiu-Ruse sau Vama Veche-Durankulak). Cu autocarul: curse regulate din 10+ orașe românești, de la 30-50 EUR dus-întors. Cu avionul: zbor charter București → Burgas (45 minute, de la 80 EUR dus-întors).

---

## Vacanță cu Copiii în Europa 2026: 10 Destinații, Buget Real și Tot ce Trebuie să Știi

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/city-breaks/vacanta-cu-copiii-europa-2026
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** city-breaks
**Publicat:** 2026-07-30
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-30

**Descriere:** Ghid complet pentru familii: cele mai bune destinații europene pentru copii în 2026 cu prețuri reale, activități pe grupe de vârstă, sfaturi practice și tot ce nu găsești în broșuri.

**Rezumat rapid:** Cele mai bune destinații europene pentru familii cu copii în 2026: Antalya all-inclusive (1.200–2.500 EUR pentru 2 adulți + 2 copii, 7 nopți cu zbor), Creta (plaje cu apă de genunchi, perfecte sub 6 ani), Barcelona (Aquarium + Park Güell + plajă), Budapesta (termalele cu tobogane), Viena (Schönbrunn Zoo + Prater), Croazieră MSC (copii sub 12 ani gratuit pe multe date), și România (Peleș + Transilvania, cel mai ieftin). Regula esențială: o atracție dimineața + piscină/plajă după-amiază. Mai mult de atât și vacanța devine marș forțat.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Care e cea mai ieftină destinație europeană pentru familii?**
R: Antalya all-inclusive bate orice altă destinație europeană pe raport calitate-preț pentru familii: 1.200–1.800 EUR total pentru 2 adulți + 2 copii, 7 nopți cu zbor inclus. Copiii sub 12 ani au reduceri de 30–70% la majoritate hotelurilor. All-inclusive elimină complet costul meselor și al băuturilor.

**Î: De la ce vârstă merită vacanța cu avionul?**
R: Nu există vârstă minimă, dar practic: sub 18 luni — destinații scurte (1–2 ore de zbor), mai ales cu all-inclusive unde nu trebuie să explorezi activ. 2–5 ani — orice destinație cu plajă sau aquapark. 6–12 ani — orice destinație, inclusiv city breaks culturale moderate. Peste 12 ani — pot participa activ la toate tipurile de experiențe.

**Î: Croaziera cu copiii — merită față de all-inclusive?**
R: Depinde de vârsta copilului. Sub 3 ani: all-inclusive e mai comod — rutina contează. 3–17 ani: croaziera e adesea mai bună — despachetezi o singură dată, copiii au activități non-stop la clubul de copii, și văd 4–5 destinații fără logistică. MSC oferă copii gratis sub 12 ani pe multe date.

**Î: Câte activități planifici pe zi cu copiii?**
R: Maximum o atracție majoră dimineața + timp liber (plajă/piscină) după-amiaza. Tentația de a 'profita' de fiecare oră din vacanță duce la copii epuizați și crize la 15:00. Vacanta de familie nu e tur cultural — e recuperare pentru toată familia.

**Î: All-inclusive sau hotel cu mic dejun — ce aleg cu copiii mici?**
R: All-inclusive câștigă clar cu copii sub 10 ani: elimini complet anxietatea meselor (copilul pretențios mănâncă întotdeauna ceva din bufet), nu ai costuri variabile surpriză, și nu cauți restaurante cu meniu pentru copii în fiecare seară. Peste 10 ani, hotel cu mic dejun deschide mai mult explorarea autentică a destinației.

**Î: Ce asigurare aleg pentru o vacanță cu copiii?**
R: Poliță de familie (2 adulți + copiii) — 30–60 EUR/săptămână, mai ieftină decât polițe individuale separate. Verifică: (1) acoperire medicală minimă 30.000 EUR, (2) anularea călătoriei inclusă (copiii se îmbolnăvesc brusc înaintea plecării), (3) însoțitorul acoperit dacă copilul e internat. Pentru Turcia: asigurarea e obligatorie, CEASS nu funcționează acolo.

**Î: Pașaport sau buletin pentru copii în Europa?**
R: Cetățenii UE pot călători în interiorul UE cu carte de identitate. Turcia, UK și destinațiile non-UE cer pașaport. Copiii sub 14 ani nu au buletin — au nevoie de pașaport pentru orice călătorie internațională. Pașaportul pentru copii e valabil 3 ani (sub 14 ani) sau 5 ani (14–18 ani). Planifică reînoirile din timp.

**Î: Ce fac cu bagajele pe aeroportul Heathrow sau CDG cu copii mici?**
R: Strategie: doi adulți, distribuție clară — unul cu copiii, unul cu bagajele. Caruciorul sau rucsacul-transport pentru bebeluși e prioritar dacă copilul nu merge. Fii la poartă cu 30 de minute înainte de boarding — familiile cu copii mici boarding primii la Wizz Air și Ryanair (verifică politica specifică).

---

## Vacanță în Egipt 2026: piramide, Marea Roșie, croazieră pe Nil — ghid complet cu prețuri reale

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/cazari/vacanta-egipt-2026-ghid-complet
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** cazari
**Publicat:** 2026-07-16
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-16

**Descriere:** Tot ce trebuie să știi despre o vacanță în Egipt. Piramidele, Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh, croazieră pe Nil, vize, siguranță, și bugetul real pentru români.

**Rezumat rapid:** O vacanță all-inclusive în Egipt (7 nopți Hurghada cu zbor charter) pornește de la 400 EUR/persoană. Piramidele de la Giza + Sfinxul: 20 USD intrare. Croazieră pe Nil (4 nopți Luxor-Aswan): de la 350 EUR/persoană. Viză la sosire: 25 USD (sticker visa la aeroport). Pașaport obligatoriu (valabil 6 luni). eSIM recomandat — roaming e foarte scump. Asigurare obligatorie. Cel mai bun sezon: octombrie-aprilie (vara e 40-45°C la piramide).

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Am nevoie de viză pentru Egipt?**
R: Da. Românii au nevoie de viză. Cea mai simplă opțiune: viză la sosire (visa on arrival) — 25 USD, se cumpără la ghișeul de vize din aeroport (înainte de imigrări). Se plătește în USD cash (ia bancnote exacte). Alternativ: e-visa online (25 USD, pe visa2egypt.gov.eg), procesare 7 zile. Pașaport valabil 6 luni obligatoriu.

**Î: E sigur să călătorești în Egipt?**
R: Zonele turistice (Cairo, Giza, Luxor, Aswan, Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh) sunt sigure, cu prezență de securitate vizibilă. Evită: Peninsula Sinai (excepție: Sharm el-Sheikh), zona de graniță cu Libia, și zonele rurale izolate. Folosește ghizi locali licențiați pentru excursii la piramide — evită 'ajutorul' nesolicitat.

**Î: Care e cel mai bun sezon pentru Egipt?**
R: Octombrie-aprilie: temperaturi plăcute (20-28°C la Cairo), ideale pentru vizitare. Mai-septembrie: 38-45°C la piramide — extrem de greu de suportat. Hurghada și Sharm el-Sheikh sunt suportabile tot anul (brezee de mare), dar activitățile culturale (piramide, Luxor) sunt imposibile vara.

---

## Vacanță în Portugalia 2026: Lisabona, Porto și Algarve — Ghid Complet cu Bugete Reale

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/city-breaks/vacanta-portugalia-2026-lisabona-porto-algarve
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** city-breaks
**Publicat:** 2026-07-30
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-30

**Descriere:** Ghid vacanță Portugalia 2026: Lisabona, Porto și Algarve. Prețuri reale, itinerar 10 zile, cele mai bune plaje și sfaturi practice pentru o călătorie reușită.

**Rezumat rapid:** Portugalia e cel mai bun raport calitate-preț din Europa de Vest în 2026. Buget zilnic: 55–80 EUR (față de 90–120 EUR în Spania sau Italia pentru experiențe echivalente). Lisabona: tramvaiul 28, pastéis de nata la 1.20 EUR, Alfama și miradouros gratuite, Sintra la 40 minute cu trenul. Porto: cramele de vin Port (degustare 10–20 EUR), Francesinha, Ribeira UNESCO, cel mai bun pește grătar din Europa. Algarve: stânci de calcar auriu, Benagil Sea Cave, plajele Praia da Marinha și Ponta da Piedade. Zbor din București de la 70 EUR. Mașina închiriată e obligatorie pentru Algarve.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Câte zile îți trebuie în Portugalia?**
R: Minimum 5 zile pentru Lisabona + Sintra + Porto. Ideal 10 zile pentru tot: 3 zile Lisabona + Sintra + 3 zile Porto + 3 zile Algarve. Dacă ai un singur weekend: alege Lisabona SAU Porto — nu ambele în 3 zile, graba omoară experiența.

**Î: Lisabona sau Porto — care e mai bună?**
R: Lisabona: mai mare, cosmopolită, plaje accesibile la 30 min cu trenul, viață de noapte mai intensă. Porto: mai mică, mai autentică, mai ieftină cu 20–30%, mâncare mai bună, vinuri Port în crame cu vedere la Douro. Dacă poți: fă-le pe amândouă — trenul rapid durează 2h30 și costă 25 EUR.

**Î: E Portugalia mai ieftină decât Spania?**
R: Da, semnificativ — mai ales Porto față de Barcelona sau Madrid. Cafea: 0.80–1.20 EUR (față de 2–3 EUR în Spania). Masă completă: 8–14 EUR (față de 12–18 EUR). Cazare 3 stele: 50–90 EUR/noapte (față de 80–130 EUR). Buget zilnic în Porto: 45–65 EUR față de 70–100 EUR în Barcelona.

**Î: Când e cel mai bun moment să mergi în Portugalia?**
R: Mai–iunie și septembrie–octombrie: vreme excelentă (22–28°C), cozi minime, prețuri rezonabile. Iulie–august: cald (28–35°C în Algarve), aglomerat și mai scump — dar totuși sub nivelul altor destinații mediteraneene. Iarna: Lisabona și Porto sunt plăcute (15–18°C), Algarve devine liniștit și foarte ieftin.

**Î: Trebuie mașină închiriată în Portugalia?**
R: Depinde de program. Lisabona și Porto: nu — metrou, tramvai și mersul pe jos acoperă tot. Sintra: tren din Rossio (4.70 EUR, 40 min). Algarve: DA — obligatoriu. Plajele Algarve sunt împrăștiate pe 150 km de coastă și nu există transport public eficient între ele.

**Î: E sigură Portugalia pentru turiști?**
R: Portugalia e constant în top 5 cele mai sigure țări din lume (Global Peace Index). Principalul risc: furtul din buzunare pe tramvaiul 28 și în zonele turistice aglomerate din Alfama. Folosiți genți crossbody și aveți grijă în locuri aglomerate. Altfel: relaxat, prietenos, fără probleme.

**Î: Ce mânânci obligatoriu în Portugalia?**
R: Pastéis de nata (1.20 EUR, Pastéis de Belém sau Manteigaria), Francesinha în Porto (sos de bere picant, brânză topită, straturi de carne — 8–10 EUR), pește grătar la Matosinhos (12–18 EUR), bacalhau à Brás (cod cu ouă și cartofi — 8–12 EUR), ginjinha (lichior de vișine — 1.50 EUR la stand).

**Î: Ai nevoie de eSIM sau asigurare în Portugalia?**
R: Portugalia e în UE — roaming gratuit cu orice abonament românesc, CEASS funcționează pentru urgențe la spitalele publice. eSIM nu e necesar. O poliță completă de asigurare (15 EUR/săptămână) adaugă repatriere, anulare și bagaje — recomandat dar nu obligatoriu ca în Turcia sau UK.

## Vacanță în Turcia 2026: e sigur, ce spune MAE și ce trebuie să știi înainte de plecare

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/asigurari/vacanta-turcia-2026-siguranta
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** asigurari
**Publicat:** 2026-07-09

**Descriere:** Situația actuală în Turcia pentru turiști în 2026, recomandările MAE, zonele de evitat și sfaturi practice pentru Antalya, Istanbul și coasta turcă.

**Rezumat rapid:** Zonele turistice din Turcia (Antalya, Istanbul, coasta Egeei) sunt considerate sigure pentru turiști în 2026, conform recomandărilor MAE. Ministerul Afacerilor Externe recomandă evitarea zonelor de sud-est ale Turciei, la granița cu Iran, Siria și Irak. Stațiunile de pe coasta mediteraneană și Egee (Antalya, Bodrum, Marmaris, Alanya) sunt la sute de kilometri de zonele de conflict și funcționează normal.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Antalya e sigura in 2026?**
R: Da. Antalya se află pe coasta mediteraneană, la circa 1.200 km distanță față de granița cu Siria și Irak. MAE nu recomandă evitarea Antalyei sau a coastei mediteraneene. Stațiunile turistice (Kemer, Side, Alanya, Belek) funcționează normal, cu flux turistic internațional neafectat.

**Î: Ce zone din Turcia trebuie evitate?**
R: MAE recomandă evitarea zonelor de sud-est, la frontiera cu Iran, Siria și Irak: provinciile Hatay, Gaziantep (parțial), Sanliurfa, Mardin, Sirnak, Hakkari, Van și zona kurdă. Acestea sunt la 800-1500 km distanță față de stațiunile turistice populare.

**Î: Turcia e in UE? Am nevoie de asigurare?**
R: Nu, Turcia nu e în UE. Roamingul UE nu se aplică — vei fi taxat de operatorul român la tarife non-UE (10-15 EUR/GB). Ia un eSIM prepaid înainte de plecare. Asigurarea de călătorie e obligatorie moral — sistemul medical turcesc e bun dar scump pentru turiști fără asigurare.

**Î: Cum aflu situatia actuala inainte de plecare?**
R: Verifică mae.ro (secțiunea Călătorii/Avertizări) cu câteva zile înainte de plecare pentru ultimele actualizări. MAE actualizează avertizările în timp real. Înregistrează-te pe platforma MAE pentru români în străinătate (cetateniinostri.mae.ro) dacă rămâi mai mult de câteva zile.

**Î: Ce fac dacă zborul spre Turcia e anulat din cauza situației?**
R: Dacă compania aeriană anulează zborul din motive de securitate sau forță majoră, ai dreptul la refund complet sau redirecționare pe alt zbor. Dacă tu anulezi voluntar, depinde de condițiile biletului. Asigurarea cu clauza de anulare acoperă anularea din motive de forță majoră — verifică termenii poliței tale.

---

## Veneția 2026: Ghid Complet — San Marco, Palatul Dogilor, Gondole, Vaporetto și Ce Nu Îți Spune Nimeni

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/city-breaks/venetia-ghid-complet-2026
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** city-breaks
**Publicat:** 2026-07-31
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-31
**Traducere a:** [venice-complete-guide-2026](https://plecari.com/ro/city-breaks/venice-complete-guide-2026)

**Descriere:** Ghid complet Veneția 2026. Canale, gondole, taxa turistică, când să mergi, cartierele mai puțin aglomerate și sfaturi practice pentru prima vizită.

**Rezumat rapid:** Veneția e construită pe 118 insule legate prin 150+ canale și 400+ poduri, fără mașini — totul se mișcă pe apă sau pe jos. Noutate 2026: taxa de acces (Contributo di Accesso) pentru VIZITATORII DE ZI se aplică în zilele cu cerere mare — €5 dacă rezervi în avans pe veneziaunica.it, €10 pe loc. Oaspeții care stau overnight sunt EXCEPTAȚI. Vaporetto: €9.50 cursă unică, €25/24 ore. Gondola: €90 (30 min, ziua). Bazilica San Marco: €12–15 (rezervare în avans). Palatul Dogilor: €30 (Itinerarul Secret €32). Cel mai bun moment: octombrie–mai pentru mai puțini turiști.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Trebuie să plătesc taxa de acces în Veneția 2026?**
R: Doar dacă ești vizitator de zi (ajungi și pleci în aceeași zi) în zilele de vârf desemnate. Taxa e €5 rezervată în avans pe veneziaunica.it sau €10 pe loc. Amendă pentru nerespectare: €50–300. Dacă stai overnight în Veneția, ești EXCEPTAT — plătești în schimb taxa turistică hotelieră (€1–5/persoană/noapte, separat la check-in). Taxa se aplică în principal în weekenduri și sărbători italiene între aprilie și iulie.

**Î: Cum mă deplasez în Veneția?**
R: Pe jos și cu vaporetto (autobuzul de apă). Veneția nu are mașini — e un oraș pietonal conectat prin 400+ poduri. Majoritatea obiectivelor majore sunt la 20–25 minute de mers pe jos unele de altele. Vaporetto acoperă distanțe mai lungi: Linia 1 merge pe tot traseul Marelui Canal (scenic, lent); Linia 2 e mai rapidă. Cursă unică: €9.50. Pass 24h: €25. 48h: €35. 72h: €45.

**Î: Ce este Itinerarul Secret al Palatului Dogilor?**
R: Turul Itinerariul Secret (Itinerari Segreti) te duce prin zone închise vizitatorilor obișnuiți: camera de tortură, birourile inchizitorilor de stat, și celebra închisoare Piombi din acoperiș din care Casanova a evadat în 1756 — singura evadare reușită din Piombi. Tur ghidat de 75 minute, €32. Se epuizează cu săptămâni înainte — rezervare la palazzoducale.visitmuve.it.

**Î: Cât costă o gondolă în Veneția 2026?**
R: Tarif oficial fix: €90 pentru 30 de minute (ziua, maxim 5 pasageri), €110 după ora 19:00. Nu se negociază — tariful e reglementat municipal. Gondola nu e un mijloc de transport — e o experiență ceremonială. Pentru deplasare, folosiți vaporetto. Cea mai bună gondolă: pe canalele mici (rii), nu pe Marele Canal — 25–30 minute prin pasaje umbrite, pe sub poduri joase.

**Î: Ce sunt cicchetti și bacari?**
R: Cicchetti sunt tradiția culinară emblematică a Veneției — mâncăruri mici servite la bacari (baruri tradiționale de vin) pe tot parcursul zilei. Gândiți-vă la ele ca la tapas venețiene: baccalà mantecato (cod sărat bătut pe pâine), sarde in saor (sardine dulci-acre cu stafide și nuci de pin), polpette (chifteluțe), crostini cu diverse toppinguri. Mănânci în picioare la bar cu o ombra (un pahar mic de vin local, €1.50–2.50). Fondamenta della Misericordia din Cannaregio e cea mai bună stradă pentru cicchetti.

**Î: Ce este acqua alta și când se întâmplă?**
R: Acqua alta (apă mare) e inundarea periodică a zonelor joase din Veneție — cel mai frecvent Piazza San Marco. Se întâmplă cel mai des octombrie–ianuarie. Când e prevăzut acqua alta, orașul instalează passerele (poduri de lemn ridicate). Poți traversa cu încălțăminte impermeabilă sau cu acoperitori (soprascarpe) cumpărabile la €5–10. Bariertele MOSE (operaționale complet din 2023) au redus dramatic frecvența și severitatea evenimentelor majore.

**Î: Ce insule merită vizitate din Veneția?**
R: Murano (capitala suflării în sticlă, 7 min cu vaporetto), Burano (casele colorate, dantelărie, 40 min), și Torcello (cea mai veche așezare din lagună, catedrală bizantină extraordinară, 50 min) sunt principalele. Lido (insula plajă a Veneției, 20 min) merită vara. Vaporetto acoperă toate insulele — Linii 3, 4, 12 de la Fondamente Nove.

---

## Zbor anulat sau întârziat în 2026: drepturile tale, compensații de până la 600 EUR și cum recuperezi banii

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/zboruri/zbor-anulat-intarziat-drepturi-compensatii
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** zboruri
**Publicat:** 2026-07-13
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-13

**Descriere:** Ghid complet despre drepturile pasagerilor aerieni în UE. Ce compensații primești pentru zbor anulat sau întârziat, cum ceri despăgubirea, și ce s-a schimbat în regulamentul EU261 în 2026.

**Rezumat rapid:** Dacă zborul tău a fost anulat sau întârziat cu peste 3 ore, ai dreptul la compensație de 250-600 EUR conform Regulamentului EU261. Suma depinde de distanța zborului: 250 EUR (sub 1.500 km), 400 EUR (1.500-3.500 km), 600 EUR (peste 3.500 km). Compania aeriană NU trebuie să te despăgubească doar dacă întârzierea e cauzată de circumstanțe extraordinare (vreme extremă, grevă ATC, securitate). Ai 3 ani să depui cererea. Poți face cererea singur sau prin servicii specializate precum AirHelp (comision doar dacă câștigi).

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Cât primesc compensație pentru un zbor anulat?**
R: Compensația e fixă, bazată pe distanța zborului, NU pe prețul biletului: 250 EUR pentru zboruri sub 1.500 km (ex: București-Budapesta), 400 EUR pentru 1.500-3.500 km (ex: București-Londra), 600 EUR pentru peste 3.500 km (ex: București-New York). Primești aceeași sumă indiferent dacă biletul a costat 30 EUR sau 300 EUR.

**Î: Compania aeriană poate refuza despăgubirea?**
R: Da, doar dacă demonstrează 'circumstanțe extraordinare' — situații în afara controlului lor: vreme extremă (furtună, ceață densă), greve ale controlorilor de trafic aerian (NU greve ale personalului companiei — alea NU sunt circumstanțe extraordinare), amenințări de securitate, sau instabilitate politică. Probleme tehnice ale aeronavei NU sunt circumstanțe extraordinare — Curtea Europeană de Justiție a confirmat asta.

**Î: Cât timp am să depun cererea?**
R: 3 ani de la data zborului (conform legislației română). Asta înseamnă că poți cere compensație retroactiv pentru zboruri din 2023-2026. Nu amâna — dovezile se pierd și companiile fac mai greu reconstituirea.

**Î: Pot cere compensație și pentru zboruri low-cost (Wizz Air, Ryanair)?**
R: Da. Regulamentul EU261 se aplică TUTUROR companiilor aeriene care operează zboruri din/în UE, indiferent de tipul biletului. Wizz Air, Ryanair, Blue Air, Tarom — toate sunt obligate legal să plătească. Tipul biletului (promo, standard, business) nu contează — compensația e aceeași.

**Î: Merită să folosesc un serviciu precum AirHelp?**
R: Dacă nu ai timp sau energie să te ocupi singur (companiile aeriene trag de timp și refuză frecvent cererile legitime), da. AirHelp se ocupă de tot procesul, inclusiv acțiunea în instanță dacă e necesar. Comisionul: 35% din compensație, doar dacă câștigi. Dacă nu câștigi, nu plătești nimic. Calculul: 400 EUR compensație - 35% comision = 260 EUR net pentru tine, fără niciun efort.

---

## Zbor cu Escală vs. Direct 2026: Când Merită Conexiunea și Când Nu

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/zboruri/zbor-cu-escala-vs-direct
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** zboruri
**Publicat:** 2026-07-30
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-30

**Descriere:** Ghid complet: cât economisești cu zborul cu escală pe rute europene și intercontinentale, riscurile reale, hub-urile fiabile, cum te protejezi dacă pierzi conexiunea și escala lungă ca bonus.

**Rezumat rapid:** Pe rute europene scurte (sub 4 ore direct), zborul direct câștigă aproape întotdeauna — economia cu escala e minimă (10–30 EUR) și nu justifică riscul și timpul adăugat. Pe rute intercontinentale (SUA, Asia, Africa), escala poate economisi 200–500 EUR — diferență care justifică 3–5 ore de drum suplimentar. Regula de bază: același bilet (PNR unic), minimum 90 minute escală intra-UE sau 2–3 ore internațional, hub fiabil (Istanbul, Viena, Amsterdam). Cu bilete separate ești pe cont propriu dacă pierzi conexiunea.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Merită zborul cu escală față de direct?**
R: Pe rute europene (sub 4 ore de zbor): rareori — economia e 10–30 EUR dar adaugi 2–4 ore de drum și risc de conexiune ratată. Pe rute intercontinentale (8+ ore de zbor): frecvent da — economii de 200–500 EUR justifică 3–5 ore suplimentare. Formula: economie reală ÷ ore pierdute = valoare per oră. Dacă depășește 50 EUR/oră, escala merită.

**Î: Ce se întâmplă dacă pierd conexiunea?**
R: Cu un singur bilet (PNR unic): compania te pune pe următorul zbor disponibil fără cost suplimentar, acoperă masa și cazarea dacă e necesar, și ești eligibil EU261 cu 3+ ore întârziere la destinație (250–600 EUR compensație). Cu bilete separate: ești pe cont propriu — trebuie să cumperi bilet nou la prețul momentului, care poate fi 500–1.200 EUR pentru intercontinentale.

**Î: Care e timpul minim de escală recomandat?**
R: Minimum 90 minute pentru conexiuni intra-UE pe hub-uri eficiente (Viena, Amsterdam). Minimum 2 ore pentru conexiuni internaționale. Minimum 3 ore dacă schimbi aeroportul (Heathrow↔Gatwick, CDG↔Orly). Un zbor întârziat 45 de minute e frecvent — ai nevoie de buffer real, nu de minimul teoretic.

**Î: Bagajele se transferă automat la escală?**
R: Da, dacă ai un singur bilet (același PNR). Bagajele merg direct la destinația finală — nu le ridici la escală. Cu bilete separate, trebuie să ridici bagajele, să treci prin vamă și să le re-check-in — minimum 2–3 ore necesare. Sfat: cu bilete separate, călătorește cu bagaj de mână pentru a elimina complet această problemă.

**Î: Ce hub-uri sunt fiabile pentru escale?**
R: Cele mai fiabile: Istanbul IST (Turkish Airlines, modern și eficient), Viena VIE (mic, organizat, Lufthansa Group), Dubai DXB (Emirates, excelent spre Asia-Pacific). Acceptabile: Amsterdam AMS, Frankfurt FRA. Problematice: Londra Heathrow LHR (aglomerat, multe întârzieri), Paris CDG (transfer între terminale lent).

**Î: Ce e open-jaw și merită?**
R: Open-jaw înseamnă zbori dus la o destinație și te întorci din alta (ex. București→Roma dus, Barcelona→București întors). Explorezi două orașe fără să repeți traseul. Costul e similar cu un dus-întors standard dar experiența e semnificativ mai bogată. Kiwi.com caută automat combinații open-jaw.

**Î: Escala lungă de 8 ore merită ieșit din aeroport?**
R: Absolut. Istanbul cu 6 ore: Sultanahmet și Marele Bazar la 38 minute cu metroul. Amsterdam cu 5 ore: canalele și Jordaan la 15 minute cu trenul. Viena cu 6 ore: Ringstrasse și o cafea vieneză la 16 minute cu S-Bahn. Turkish Airlines și Emirates au programe oficiale de stopover cu hotel inclus.

**Î: Asigurarea de călătorie acoperă conexiunea ratată?**
R: Numai dacă polița are acoperire explicită 'missed connection' sau 'travel delay'. Această clauză acoperă costul biletului nou dacă pierzi conexiunea din motive independente (zbor întârziat, nu pentru că ai plecat prea târziu la aeroport). Verifică polița înainte de cumpărare, mai ales pentru zboruri intercontinentale cu bilete separate.

---

## Zboruri Populare din București 2026: Rute, Prețuri Reale și Când să Rezervi

**URL:** https://plecari.com/ro/zboruri/zboruri-populare-din-bucuresti
**Limbă:** Română
**Verticală:** zboruri
**Publicat:** 2026-07-30
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-30

**Descriere:** Ghid complet pentru zborurile din București Otopeni în 2026. Top 15 rute, prețuri medii verificate, cele mai bune perioade de rezervare, Wizz Air vs Ryanair vs TAROM și cum eviți costurile ascunse.

**Rezumat rapid:** Cele mai populare zboruri din București sunt spre Londra, Roma, Istanbul, Barcelona, Paris, Amsterdam, Dublin și Atena. Prețuri medii dus-întors în sezon mediu: Roma 60–130 EUR, Istanbul 50–120 EUR, Londra 80–180 EUR, Barcelona 80–180 EUR. Cel mai ieftin moment: rezervi cu 6–8 săptămâni înainte, zboruri marți–joi, în afara vacanțelor școlare. Wizz Air are cele mai multe destinații directe (60+), Ryanair crește rapid pe București cu 35+ destinații noi din 2024–2025.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Care e cea mai ieftină destinație din București?**
R: Budapesta și Roma sunt constant cele mai ieftine: bilete de la 35–45 EUR dus-întors cu Wizz Air. Budapesta are avantajul distanței scurte (1h20 zbor) și prețuri locale mici. Roma și Bari concurează pe locul 2, mai ales în extrasezon. Istanbul e cea mai ieftină destinație non-UE (de la 50 EUR).

**Î: Wizz Air sau Ryanair din București — care e mai ieftin?**
R: Depinde de rută și dată. Wizz Air are mai multe destinații directe din București (60+ față de 35+ Ryanair) și câștigă pe rutele spre Europa de Est și Balcani. Ryanair e mai competitiv pe Roma (Ciampino), Milano (Bergamo) și Londra (Stansted/Luton). Sfat esențial: compară mereu ambele pe un motor de căutare — niciodată direct pe site-ul companiei, pentru că nu se arată reciproc.

**Î: Când e cel mai ieftin să zbori din București?**
R: Lunile cu cele mai mici prețuri: noiembrie, ianuarie și februarie (fără Crăciun/Revelion). Primăvara (martie–mai) și toamna (septembrie–octombrie) sunt sweet-spot-ul: prețuri bune + vreme excelentă la destinații mediteraneene. Iulie–august sunt cele mai scumpe, cu vârfuri în vacanța de vară.

**Î: Cât costă bagajul la Wizz Air din București?**
R: Bagaj de mână mic (40×30×20 cm): gratuit la orice bilet. Bagaj de mână extins (troler mic, cu WIZZ Priority): 6–15 EUR adăugat la rezervare. Bagaj de cală 20 kg: 20–45 EUR per segment (mai ieftin adăugat la rezervare, mai scump la check-in). Un bilet de 40 EUR cu bagaj de cală dus-întors = 80–130 EUR total — compară mereu prețul final, nu tariful de bază.

**Î: TAROM sau Wizz Air — care e mai bun?**
R: Depinde de ce prioritizezi. Wizz Air: mai ieftin pe bilet, bagajul de cală e extra, fără mese la bord, mai puțin confortabil. TAROM: bagaj de cală inclus în tarif, masă la bord pe zborurile lungi, mai multe conexiuni prin hub, și biletul afișat e prețul final. Compară PREȚUL TOTAL (cu bagaje), nu tariful de bază — diferența reală e adesea mai mică decât pare.

**Î: Există zboruri directe din București spre SUA sau Asia?**
R: Nu direct din București în 2026. Toate zborurile intercontinentale necesită escală. Cele mai bune conexiuni: Turkish Airlines prin Istanbul (Ataturk sau Sabiha Gökçen) spre toată Asia, Africa, Orientul Mijlociu; Lufthansa prin Frankfurt spre SUA și Asia; KLM prin Amsterdam spre America de Nord; Emirates prin Dubai spre Asia-Pacific și Africa.

**Î: Ce e promo Wizz Air și cum îl activez?**
R: Promo Wizz Air (Wizz Discount Club) e un abonament anual de aproximativ 30–40 EUR care oferă reduceri de 10–40 EUR pe bilet. Merită dacă zbori de 3+ ori pe an cu Wizz Air — amortizezi abonamentul după 2–3 zboruri. Activat din app sau site la cumpărarea unui bilet.

---

## Airport Transfer Guide 2026: Cheapest Ways from Airport to City at Europe's Top Destinations

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/city-breaks/airport-transfer-guide
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** city-breaks
**Publicat:** 2026-07-31
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-31
**Traducere a:** [transfer-aeroport-ghid](https://plecari.com/ro/city-breaks/transfer-aeroport-ghid)

**Descriere:** Metro, bus, train, or taxi — how to choose the best airport transfer at Rome, Paris, London, Barcelona, Istanbul, Athens, Budapest and more. Real prices, journey times, and the scams to avoid.

**Rezumat rapid:** The cheapest airport transfer is almost always the direct metro or train (€3–15). Official taxis cost 3–10× more. Uber and Bolt are cheaper than local taxis in most European cities. Never take unofficial taxis offered inside the terminal — they operate at 3–5× the official rate and have no accountability. Install Bolt or Uber before landing, have your eSIM active, and know the train/metro option for your specific airport before you arrive.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: What's the cheapest airport transfer in Europe?**
R: Metro or direct train — always check this first. It's 3–10× cheaper than a taxi, faster than a bus (no traffic), and available at virtually every major European airport. Rome Fiumicino to city centre: €8–14 by train vs €50 taxi. London Heathrow: £6 by Piccadilly Line vs £60–90 black cab. Paris CDG: €11 by RER vs €55 taxi. The metro/train is the right choice in almost every case unless you have heavy luggage, are arriving very late at night, or are travelling with children.

**Î: Uber or taxi at the airport — which is better?**
R: It depends on the city. In London, Rome, and Barcelona, Uber and Bolt are typically 20–40% cheaper than local taxis and offer transparent pricing with GPS-tracked routes. In Paris, official taxis have fixed rates to the city centre (€55 from CDG, €35 from Orly) — Uber can be similar or slightly cheaper. In Istanbul, BiTaksi and Uber both work well and are more reliable than unofficial taxis. In Athens, official taxis from the airport have fixed rates (€38–40 to city centre) and are the best option as Uber doesn't operate there.

**Î: What is a private airport transfer and is it worth it?**
R: A private transfer is a pre-booked car that meets you at arrivals with your name on a sign. Fixed price, no negotiating, no hunting for transport when you're tired. Advantages: zero stress, guaranteed price, works for late-night arrivals and families with lots of luggage. Price: typically 2–3× the taxi rate but with predictability. Worth it for: groups of 3+, families with children and strollers, arrivals after midnight, cities with unreliable taxi infrastructure. Book through GetYourGuide or Welcome Pickups for verified drivers.

**Î: Is it safe to take a taxi from the airport?**
R: Official taxis from marked stands outside the terminal: yes, safe. Unofficial drivers who approach you inside the terminal: avoid entirely. The scam works like this — someone offers 'a good price for a taxi' inside arrivals. By the time you reach the destination, the price has tripled, the meter was 'broken', or there's a surcharge for luggage, the motorway, time of day, and breathing. Use official taxi stands (marked with the city's official taxi colours), pre-booked private transfers, or ridesharing apps.

**Î: Do I need an eSIM before landing to book Uber or Bolt at the airport?**
R: Yes — this is one of the most practical reasons to have an eSIM activated before departure. The moment you land, you have data connectivity and can see Uber/Bolt prices, check train schedules, or book a transfer without hunting for airport Wi-Fi. Without data, you're dependent on airport kiosks or whatever transport is physically in front of you — often the most expensive option. Install your eSIM from Airalo or Saily at home, and it activates automatically when you land.

**Î: What's the best strategy for night arrivals at airports?**
R: For late-night arrivals (after 23:00): check if metro/train services still run (some stop between midnight and 5:00 AM), and have Uber or Bolt as a backup. Night buses exist at most major airports but are slower and less comfortable. A pre-booked private transfer is the least stressful option if you arrive after midnight — fixed price, someone waiting with your name, no uncertainty. For solo travellers comfortable with public transport, the Uber/Bolt option usually works well even late at night.

## Amalfi Coast 2026: The Complete Guide — Towns, Transport, Hiking, Food & Everything You Actually Need to Know

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/city-breaks/amalfi-coast-complete-guide-2026
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** city-breaks
**Publicat:** 2026-07-31
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-31

**Descriere:** Complete guide to the Amalfi Coast in 2026. Best towns, ferry vs road, real prices, how to avoid crowds, and where to eat in Positano, Ravello and Amalfi.

**Rezumat rapid:** The Amalfi Coast is a 50 km stretch of limestone cliffs, terraced lemon groves, and pastel-coloured towns plunging into the Tyrrhenian Sea in southern Italy, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997. Best time to visit: May–June or September (perfect weather, manageable crowds, prices 30–40% below August peak). Best base: Amalfi town — ferry and SITA bus connections to all destinations, more affordable than Positano. Transport: SITA bus (€1.50–4/journey, ticket purchased before boarding, not on the bus) or ferry (April–October, more expensive but spectacular). Driving your own car in season: avoid — ZTL restrictions are severe, fines €80–160, parking €5–10/hour.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: When is the best time to visit the Amalfi Coast?**
R: May–June and September are the golden months: warm weather (22–28°C), sea warm enough for swimming, manageable crowds, and prices 30–40% below July–August peak. September is the locals' favourite — sea temperature is at its annual maximum (26–28°C), ferries and restaurants still run at full capacity, but tourist numbers have dropped noticeably. July–August: beautiful but intense — SITA buses are packed, roads gridlocked, hotels at peak prices. October: excellent for hiking and cultural visits, some hotels and ferries begin closing. November–March: quiet, largely closed.

**Î: How do I get around the Amalfi Coast without a car?**
R: The SITA Sud bus (€1.50–4/journey) connects Sorrento, Positano, Praiano, Amalfi, Maiori, Minori, and Salerno along the SS163 road. Tickets must be purchased before boarding — at tabaccherie (tobacconists), bars, or newsagents — not on the bus. The ferry (April–October) is more expensive but dramatically more scenic: connects Salerno, Amalfi, Positano, Sorrento, and optionally Capri and Ischia. Trains reach Sorrento (from Naples via Circumvesuviana, €4) or Salerno (from Naples Trenitalia, €12–20) — then continue by SITA bus or ferry.

**Î: Can I drive the Amalfi Coast with my own car?**
R: Technically yes, but in season (June–September) it's a poor decision. ZTL (Limited Traffic Zone) restrictions are severe: Positano is closed to traffic 09:00–18:00 in summer, Ravello has permanent 24/7 ZTL, Amalfi has peak-hour restrictions. Automated cameras register number plates and fines (€80–160) arrive home via your rental company. Parking costs €5–10/hour at peak locations. Smart strategy: park at Salerno (€5/day) or Sorrento and continue by bus or ferry.

**Î: Which town is the best base on the Amalfi Coast?**
R: Amalfi town offers the best balance of accessibility, price, and experience. Ferries and SITA buses to all destinations depart from the main piazza, the 9th-century cathedral is extraordinary, there are good restaurants at reasonable prices, and Atrani (the coast's least touristed village) is a 5-minute walk east. Positano is the most photographed but most expensive and most crowded. Ravello is quiet and cultural (Villa Cimbrone, Villa Rufolo, Ravello Festival) but more isolated. Maiori and Minori offer the largest free beaches and prices 30% below Amalfi.

**Î: What is the Path of the Gods (Sentiero degli Dei) hike?**
R: The Sentiero degli Dei is a 7.8 km hiking trail from Bomerano (Agerola, 618 m elevation) to Nocelle above Positano, with continuous views of the Tyrrhenian Sea, the Li Galli archipelago (said to be Homer's Sirens islands), and the entire Amalfi Coast. Difficulty: moderate (CAI E). Duration: 3–4 hours. Recommended direction: Bomerano to Nocelle (predominantly downhill, views ahead of you). Important for July–August: mandatory advance booking (~€5) via the Parco dei Monti Lattari portal.

**Î: What are sfusato amalfitano lemons?**
R: Sfusato amalfitano is the Amalfi Coast's unique lemon variety — larger, more elongated (sfusato means 'spindle-shaped'), with an intensely fragrant, thick peel that is so sweet it can be eaten raw in salads. The name comes from the spindle-like shape. They're cultivated on terraced 'giardini di limoni' supported by chestnut poles and shade nets, forming green pergola tunnels on vertical cliff faces. The limoncello made from these lemons is categorically different from commercial varieties.

**Î: How much does a 5-night Amalfi Coast trip cost?**
R: Realistic budget for 5 nights (2 people): flights Naples return €150–250, accommodation 5 nights in Amalfi/Maiori €400–800 (3–4 star hotel), coast transport €60–100, food €300–500, experiences €100–200. Total: €1,010–1,850 for 2 people or €500–925 per person. Basing in Positano adds 40–60% to accommodation costs.

**Î: Is the Amalfi Coast worth visiting despite the crowds?**
R: Yes — with smart timing. The experience of cliffside towns, extraordinary seafood, the Path of the Gods, Villa Cimbrone's Infinity Terrace, and the lemon groves is genuinely unlike anywhere else in Europe. The key is visiting in May, June, or September rather than July–August, and accepting that this isn't a quiet secret — it's one of the world's great coastal destinations, and it's been that way since the 19th century. The crowds are real; so is everything that draws them.

**Descriere:** Everything you need for an all-inclusive holiday in Antalya 2026. Lara, Belek, Side, Kemer — which zone to choose, real costs, what ultra all-inclusive means, and excursions worth taking.

**Rezumat rapid:** A 7-night all-inclusive holiday in Antalya starts at €330/person (4-star hotel with charter flight). The four main zones: Lara (grand themed hotels, closest to airport), Belek (luxury and golf), Side (ancient ruins on the beach), and Kemer (dramatic mountains-meet-sea scenery). Ultra all-inclusive adds imported spirits, à la carte restaurants, and 24/7 snacks for €50-100 extra per person. Best months: May-June and September-October for pleasant weather without extreme heat. Turkey is NOT in the EU — travel insurance is essential, and roaming charges apply.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: What does ultra all-inclusive mean in Turkey?**
R: Ultra all-inclusive includes everything in standard AI (breakfast, lunch, dinner buffet, local drinks) PLUS: imported spirits (branded whisky, gin, vodka), unlimited à la carte restaurant access (Italian, Asian, seafood), minibar refilled daily, 24/7 snacks and ice cream, and sometimes room service. The upgrade costs €50-100 per person over standard AI for a week — worth it if you drink anything beyond Turkish beer and wine.

**Î: Is Antalya safe for tourists in 2026?**

Standard precautions apply: use hotel safes for valuables, negotiate fixed prices before taxi rides or purchases, and keep copies of your passport.

**Î: Do I need a visa for Turkey?**

**Î: Does roaming work in Turkey?**
R: Turkey is NOT in the EU, so free EU roaming does NOT apply. Your carrier will charge €3-15/day for data roaming. An eSIM for Turkey costs €4-5 for 1GB/7 days via Airalo — 10x cheaper than carrier roaming. Install before departure.

## Travel Insurance for Schengen Visa: Requirements, Coverage and How to Get It

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/asigurari/asigurare-viza-schengen
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** asigurari
**Publicat:** 2026-07-11

**Descriere:** Exact requirements for Schengen visa travel insurance: minimum €30,000 medical cover, what the policy must include, how much it costs, and what embassies check.

**Rezumat rapid:** For a short-stay Schengen visa, travel insurance is mandatory and must provide a minimum of €30,000 medical cover, be valid for the entire duration of your trip and cover all Schengen countries. It must include emergency medical expenses, medical repatriation and transport in case of death. Without this insurance, the visa is automatically refused.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Do EU citizens need Schengen travel insurance?**
R: EU citizens travelling within the EU do not need Schengen visa insurance for tourism or business. Schengen visa insurance is required for non-EU nationals (Moldovans, Ukrainians, Russians, etc.) applying for a short-stay Schengen visa, and for anyone applying for a long-stay visa (study, work, family reunification).

**Î: What do embassies check in the insurance policy?**
R: Embassies verify: the minimum cover amount (€30,000), the validity period (must cover the entire planned stay), geographic scope (all Schengen countries, not just one), and that the policy includes emergency medical expenses, repatriation and death transport. Some embassies also require the policy in English or with a certified translation.

**Î: How much does Schengen visa insurance cost?**
R: A standard Schengen policy with €30,000 cover for two weeks costs between €8 and €20, depending on age, provider and destination. The price increases with age and duration. This is a small amount compared to the real cost of medical care abroad.

**Î: Can the same insurance cover multiple trips?**
R: Yes, with an annual multi-trip policy, which covers all journeys within a year, ideal if you travel frequently. A single-trip policy covers one journey only, and is cheaper if you travel once a year. For a multiple-entry visa, the insurance must cover at least the first trip.

**Î: Does Schengen insurance cover routine doctor visits?**
R: No. Travel insurance covers unforeseen medical EMERGENCIES — accidents, acute illness, emergency hospitalisation. It does not cover routine check-ups, planned consultations or treatment for pre-existing conditions (in general). Always read the exclusions before buying.

**Î: What happens if my trip is extended beyond the policy dates?**
R: If you stay longer than the dates on your policy, you are uninsured for the additional period. You can extend some policies online before they expire. Always contact your insurer if your return is delayed — many have a 24/7 helpline for exactly this situation.

## Best eSIM for Europe 2026: Airalo vs Saily vs Yesim Compared

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/esim-roaming/best-esim-europe-2026
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** esim-roaming
**Publicat:** 2026-07-12
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-12

**Descriere:** Detailed comparison of the best eSIM providers for European travel in 2026. Airalo, Saily, and Yesim compared on price, coverage, speed, and ease of use — with real prices and practical advice.

**Rezumat rapid:** For most European travellers in 2026, Airalo offers the best balance of price, coverage and reliability — plans start at $4.50 for 1GB/7 days. Saily (by NordVPN) is slightly cheaper in some regions and includes a built-in VPN. Yesim offers the widest coverage (200+ countries) and unlimited plans but at higher prices. All three work via eSIM — no physical SIM swap needed, setup takes 2-3 minutes, and you keep your regular number for calls while using data abroad.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: What is an eSIM and how does it work?**
R: An eSIM is a digital SIM card built into your phone. Instead of swapping a physical SIM, you scan a QR code or install a profile, and you have a local data plan within 2-3 minutes. Your regular phone number stays active for calls and texts while the eSIM handles data. Most phones from 2020 onwards support eSIM (iPhone XS and later, Samsung Galaxy S20+, Google Pixel 4+).

**Î: Is eSIM better than roaming in Europe?**
R: If you're travelling within the EU with an EU SIM card, free roaming applies (with fair use limits). But if you're from the US/UK/outside EU, or your carrier charges for roaming, an eSIM is dramatically cheaper — €4-10 for a week vs €5-15 per DAY for carrier roaming. Even within the EU, an eSIM gives you a guaranteed fast data connection without worrying about fair use caps.

**Î: Can I use WhatsApp and Google Maps with an eSIM?**
R: Yes. An eSIM provides mobile data, so all data-based apps work normally: WhatsApp, Google Maps, Instagram, Uber, Bolt, Google Translate, and any other app. Calls and texts through your regular number still work via your primary SIM (you may pay roaming rates for those — use WhatsApp/FaceTime calls instead).

**Î: Do I need to unlock my phone for eSIM?**
R: No. eSIMs work independently of your physical SIM. However, your phone must support eSIM technology. Check by going to Settings > General > About and looking for 'EID' (iPhone), or Settings > Connections > SIM card manager (Android). If you see an eSIM option, you're set.

**Î: Which eSIM provider has the best coverage in Europe?**
R: All three major providers (Airalo, Saily, Yesim) cover the 30+ European countries most travellers visit. Airalo uses Vodafone and Three as primary carriers in most countries. Saily uses local tier-1 networks. Yesim has the widest raw coverage (200+ countries) which matters for multi-continent trips. For Europe-only travel, all three are equivalent in coverage.

## Bucharest in 3 Days: The Ultimate City Break Guide 2026

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/city-breaks/bucharest-city-break-guide
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** city-breaks
**Publicat:** 2026-07-12
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-12

**Descriere:** Everything you need for a Bucharest city break in 2026. Day-by-day itinerary, budget breakdown, where to eat, nightlife, Palace of Parliament, Old Town, and practical tips.

**Rezumat rapid:** Bucharest is one of Europe's best-value city breaks: a 3-day trip costs £40-60 per day including meals, transport and attractions. The Palace of Parliament (world's heaviest building), the Old Town's legendary nightlife, incredible Romanian food, and Belle Époque architecture make it genuinely surprising. Flights from London start at £25 one-way with Wizz Air or Ryanair. Beer costs €2.50, a full restaurant meal €10-15, and most museums are under €5.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Is Bucharest worth visiting?**
R: Absolutely. Bucharest surprises nearly everyone who visits. It has the world's heaviest building (Palace of Parliament), a thriving food scene with full meals for €10-15, nightlife that rivals Berlin, and Belle Époque architecture that earned it the nickname 'Little Paris'. It's also one of the cheapest capitals in Europe — beer costs €2.50, an Uber ride across the city is €3-4.

**Î: How many days do you need in Bucharest?**
R: 3 days is ideal for the city itself. Add 1-2 days if you want to do day trips to Transylvania (Peleș Castle, Brașov, or Bran Castle are all reachable by train). A weekend trip (2 nights) works if you prioritise the Old Town, Palace of Parliament, and food.

**Î: Is Bucharest safe for tourists?**
R: Yes. Bucharest is generally safe for tourists, including solo travellers. Standard precautions apply: watch for pickpockets in crowded areas (Old Town on weekend nights), use licensed taxis or ride-hailing apps (Bolt, Uber), and avoid unlicensed money changers. Violent crime targeting tourists is extremely rare.

**Î: How do I get from Bucharest airport to the city centre?**
R: Express Bus 783 runs every 15-30 minutes from Henri Coandă Airport to Piața Unirii (city centre), takes 40-50 minutes, and costs €1. Alternatively, Bolt or Uber cost €8-12 and take 25-40 minutes depending on traffic. Avoid unlicensed taxi drivers outside arrivals.

**Î: What currency does Romania use?**
R: Romanian Leu (RON). €1 ≈ 5 RON. Card payments are accepted almost everywhere in Bucharest (restaurants, shops, metro, Bolt). ATMs are widely available. Avoid exchanging money at the airport — rates are poor.

Nessebar, a UNESCO World Heritage City, is 5 minutes from Sunny Beach. The resort infrastructure has improved dramatically in recent years with newer hotels and larger aquaparks.

**Î: Do I need a passport for Bulgaria?**
R: EU citizens (including Romanians) do not need a passport — your national ID card is sufficient. Bulgaria joined Schengen in 2025, so land border crossings are seamless with no queuing. Bulgaria also adopted the euro in January 2026, so there's no currency exchange needed for European visitors.

**Î: Bulgaria or Turkey — which is better for a beach holiday?**
R: Bulgaria wins on: proximity (5 hours by car vs. 2-hour flight), price (20–30% cheaper), no passport needed for EU visitors, and no language barrier at resorts. Turkey wins on: hotel quality (generally newer and larger), more reliable weather in shoulder season, and better gastronomic diversity. For families with young children, Bulgaria is more practical. For couples wanting luxury, Turkey often edges it.

**Î: Is Sunny Beach or Sozopol better?**
R: They serve different travellers. Sunny Beach (8 km of beach, 350+ hotels, nightlife, aquaparks) is for those who want maximum animation, facilities, and entertainment. Sozopol (2,600-year-old town on a peninsula, quieter beaches, art galleries, excellent restaurants) is for those who want beauty, culture, and atmosphere. The good news: they're 30 km apart — you can stay in one and day-trip to the other.

**Î: What is Nessebar and is it worth visiting?**
R: Nessebar Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on a narrow peninsula 5 km from Sunny Beach. It has 40+ Byzantine churches (many in ruins, some intact), medieval fortifications, cobblestone streets, wooden-balconied houses, and excellent fish restaurants on the harbour. A mandatory evening visit from Sunny Beach — bus €1 or taxi €5. Plan 2–3 hours.

**Î: Can I drive to Bulgaria from Romania?**
R: Yes — this is the most popular option for Romanian families. Bucharest to Sunny Beach: ~400 km, approximately 5 hours. Cluj to Sunny Beach: ~750 km, 8–9 hours. Two main routes: via Giurgiu-Ruse (bridge over the Danube, no fee) or via the Romanian Black Sea coast (Vama Veche-Durankulak border crossing). Since Schengen accession in 2025, border crossings no longer have queues.

**Î: Do I need travel insurance for Bulgaria?**
R: Bulgaria is an EU member, so your European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) works at public hospitals. However, a full travel insurance policy (from ~€12/week) adds repatriation, trip cancellation, and baggage cover that EHIC doesn't include. At these prices, it's always worth having.

## Cabin Baggage Rules 2026: Wizz Air, Ryanair, British Airways and the New Liquids Rule

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/zboruri/cabin-baggage-rules-2026
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** zboruri
**Publicat:** 2026-07-29
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-29
**Traducere a:** [bagaj-mana-dimensiuni-reguli-2026](https://plecari.com/ro/zboruri/bagaj-mana-dimensiuni-reguli-2026)

**Descriere:** Exact cabin baggage dimensions for major airlines in 2026, the new liquids rule at UK and EU airports, and how to avoid €50–100 gate fees for oversized bags.

**Rezumat rapid:** Wizz Air free bag: 40×30×20 cm under the seat. Trolley in overhead bin requires Wizz Priority (extra charge) — without it, trolleys are taken at the gate and charged €50–100. Ryanair free bag: 40×20×25 cm under the seat. Overhead bin requires Priority Boarding. British Airways and full-service carriers: one cabin bag plus a personal item allowed free for all passengers. New in 2026 at many UK and EU airports: the 100ml liquid restriction has been lifted for airports with new CT scanners — but verify for each airport, as the rule still applies where old scanners remain.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Can I bring a trolley on Wizz Air for free?**
R: No. Wizz Air's free baggage allowance is a single personal item of 40×30×20 cm that must fit under the seat. Trolleys (overhead bin-size bags) are only permitted with WIZZ Priority, which costs extra. Without Priority, trolleys are confiscated at the gate and sent to the hold for a fee of €50–100. If you plan to take a trolley on board, add WIZZ Priority online when booking — it costs less than the gate fee.

**Î: What is the difference between Wizz Air and Ryanair baggage allowances?**
R: Both allow one free personal item under the seat: Wizz Air allows 40×30×20 cm (wider), Ryanair allows 40×20×25 cm (narrower but taller). Both require an upgrade (Wizz Priority / Ryanair Priority Boarding) to bring a trolley into the overhead bin. Ryanair's free bag is noticeably narrower — a bag that fits Wizz Air may not fit Ryanair. Always measure before travelling.

**Î: Has the 100ml liquid rule changed in 2026?**
R: At airports with new CT scanners (including London Heathrow, Manchester, most major UK airports as of 2024, and selected EU airports), the 100ml restriction has been lifted — you can carry larger liquid containers and do not need to remove them from your bag. However, the old 100ml rule still applies at airports that have not yet upgraded their scanning equipment. Always check the specific airport before travelling.

**Î: What is the maximum weight for cabin baggage?**
R: Wizz Air: 10 kg for the personal item or Priority bag. Ryanair: 10 kg for the Priority trolley (the free item has no specified weight limit but must fit under the seat). British Airways: 23 kg combined for cabin bag plus personal item. Full-service carriers typically allow 7–12 kg. Note that cabin baggage weight limits are enforced less rigorously than hold baggage, but overweight bags at the gate are sent to the hold at standard hold baggage prices.

**Î: Can I bring a backpack AND a trolley on a Ryanair flight?**
R: Only with Priority Boarding. Without Priority: you can bring one bag only (40×20×25 cm, under the seat). With Priority: one trolley (55×40×20 cm, overhead bin) PLUS one small personal item (under the seat). Attempting to board with both items without Priority Boarding results in one item being gate-checked.

**Î: Are wheels and handles included in the bag dimensions?**
R: Yes, always. Bag dimensions include wheels, handles, side pockets, and any extension when the handle is retracted. A trolley advertised as '55 cm' may measure 58 cm with the handle base — measure your actual bag before travel. The sizer gauges at check-in use real dimensions including all protrusions.

**Î: What items must I always carry in cabin baggage?**
R: Passport and travel documents, prescription medication (enough for the trip plus 3 extra days), laptop and valuable electronics, cash, bank cards, keys, irreplaceable items (jewellery, family photos). The airline's liability for items lost from checked luggage is capped — valuables in the hold are lost at the standard Montreal Convention limit of approximately €1,500.

## Car Rental Documents Required in 2026: Driving Licence, Credit Card and Age Rules

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/inchirieri-auto/car-rental-documents
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** inchirieri-auto
**Publicat:** 2026-07-29
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-29
**Traducere a:** [acte-necesare-inchiriere-masina](https://plecari.com/ro/inchirieri-auto/acte-necesare-inchiriere-masina)

**Descriere:** Exactly what documents you need to rent a car: driving licence requirements, credit vs debit card rules, minimum age, young driver fees, and when you need an international driving permit.

**Rezumat rapid:** To rent a car you need three things: a valid driving licence (category B, typically held for at least 1 year), a passport or national ID for identity verification, and a credit card in the driver's name for the security deposit. Minimum age is usually 21. Drivers under 25 pay a young driver surcharge of €5–15/day. EU licence holders do not need an international driving permit within the EU. Outside the EU (USA, Turkey, Australia), an IDP is strongly recommended.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Do I need an international driving permit in Europe?**
R: No, if your driving licence was issued by an EU/EEA member state. EU licences are mutually recognised across all 27 member states plus Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein. An international driving permit (IDP) is only required if your licence was issued outside the EU/EEA, or if your licence is written in non-Latin characters (Arabic, Cyrillic, Greek, Chinese, Japanese, etc.).

**Î: Can I rent a car with a debit card?**
R: Rarely with major chains (Hertz, Avis, Europcar, Sixt). These companies almost universally require a credit card for the security deposit. Some smaller and local operators accept debit cards with additional conditions (higher deposit, age restrictions). Prepaid cards, Maestro, and Revolut Standard (debit) are almost never accepted. Revolut credit card or a traditional Visa/Mastercard credit card is the safe option.

**Î: What is the minimum age to rent a car?**
R: Most rental companies set the minimum age at 21, with a valid driving licence held for at least 1 year. Some operators require 23 or 25 for certain vehicle categories (luxury, large SUVs, automatic). Drivers under 25 typically pay a young driver surcharge of €5–15/day on top of the base rental price.

**Î: Can I use a digital driving licence on my phone?**
R: Generally no. Most rental companies require the physical driving licence card. Some EU member states have introduced digital driving licences in their apps, but rental companies have been slow to accept these — policies vary by company and country. Do not rely on a digital version when travelling abroad. Bring the physical card.

**Î: What happens to the credit card deposit when I return the car?**
R: The security deposit (typically €200–2,000 depending on car category and insurance level) is blocked — not charged — on your credit card at collection. It appears as a pending charge. When you return the car in good condition, the hold is released within 3–14 days depending on your bank. If damage is reported, the company charges some or all of the deposit against the hold.

**Î: Does my regular car insurance cover rental cars abroad?**
R: Your domestic car insurance policy covers your own vehicle, not rental cars. Some comprehensive motor insurance policies extend to rental cars in some countries — check your policy documents. Credit card travel benefits sometimes include rental car cover (Visa Infinite, Amex Gold) — but with conditions (must pay the full rental on that card, cover is secondary). A third-party excess waiver insurance is the most reliable rental cover.

**Î: Can a second driver use a rented car?**
R: Yes, but additional drivers must be added to the contract at collection and must meet all the same requirements (age, valid licence, credit card may be required). Most companies charge an additional driver fee of €3–10/day per extra driver. Some credit card rental benefits include one additional driver free — check your card terms before paying.

---

## Car Rental Without a Credit Card 2026: What Works, What Doesn't and How to Prepare

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/inchirieri-auto/car-rental-without-credit-card
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** inchirieri-auto
**Publicat:** 2026-07-30
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-30
**Traducere a:** [inchiriere-masina-fara-card-de-credit](https://plecari.com/ro/inchirieri-auto/inchiriere-masina-fara-card-de-credit)

**Descriere:** Complete guide: why rental companies require credit cards, which companies accept debit cards in Europe, how cash deposits work, whether Revolut or Wise work at the counter, and your real alternatives

**Rezumat rapid:** Renting a car without a credit card is possible but requires planning. Major chains (Hertz, Avis, Europcar, Sixt) almost universally require a credit card for the security deposit. Alternatives: local companies in Greece, Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania frequently accept debit cards or cash deposits; platforms like GetRentacar show payment policy per operator; a Revolut or N26 credit card (not debit) works like any credit card. The golden rule: confirm in writing with the company before booking — arriving at the counter without a credit card and no prior arrangement almost always ends in a refused rental.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Why do car rental companies require a credit card?**
R: The credit card enables a pre-authorisation (hold) rather than an actual charge — the deposit is blocked on the card without being withdrawn. If damage or unpaid fines occur, the company can charge the card directly. With a debit card, money is withdrawn immediately from the account, and recovering additional charges is legally and practically more complicated. It is a legal and operational distinction, not an arbitrary preference.

**Î: Does Revolut or Wise work for car rental deposits?**
R: Standard Revolut and Wise are debit cards — major chains refuse them exactly as any other debit. Revolut Metal (premium subscription) issues a physical embossed Mastercard, marginally more likely to be accepted but still classified as debit by most rental systems. Revolut Credit Card (available in selected markets) works like any credit card. Always confirm with the specific company before booking.

**Î: What happens if I arrive at the counter without a credit card?**
R: Almost certainly, the rental is refused and you lose any advance payment made. Some local companies accept a cash deposit of €300–1,500 if this was confirmed in writing in advance. Do not improvise at the counter — the time to solve this is before departure, not after a 3-hour flight with bags in hand.

**Î: Can a second driver's credit card be used for the deposit?**
R: Yes, at many companies. If a passenger travelling with you has a credit card, the deposit can be placed on their card even if the booking is in your name. Both people must be physically present at the counter. The credit card holder is added as an additional driver on the contract.

**Î: Which destinations have the most flexible policies?**
R: Local companies in Greece (islands — Crete, Rhodes, Corfu, Zakynthos), Turkey (Antalya, Bodrum), Bulgaria (Sunny Beach, Varna) and Romania are the most flexible in Europe. Many local operators in these destinations accept debit Visa/Mastercard or a cash deposit. Western Europe (France, Germany, UK) is significantly stricter.

**Î: Does car sharing work without a credit card?**
R: Yes — urban car sharing services (ShareNow, Zity, Citybee) work with debit cards and mobile apps, with no large security deposit. The limitation: car sharing is designed for urban trips, not holidays or long-distance drives. You cannot take a car sharing vehicle to a beach resort or mountain destination outside the operating zone.

**Î: What credit limit do I need on my card?**
R: The pre-authorisation (deposit hold) ranges from €200 for small economy cars to €2,000+ for luxury or premium vehicles. Your available credit limit must exceed the deposit amount — if your card has a €500 limit and the deposit is €800, the pre-authorisation fails. Check and temporarily increase your limit if necessary.

**Î: Is there a way to reduce the deposit amount?**
R: Yes. Purchasing a Super CDW or full damage waiver either at the counter or from a third-party provider (insurance4carhire.com, RentalCover.com) can reduce the deposit to zero. The third-party option costs €3–8/day versus €15–25/day at the counter. With zero excess, many companies also reduce or eliminate the pre-authorisation hold.

---

## European Health Insurance Card vs Travel Insurance: What Actually Covers You

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/asigurari/card-european-vs-asigurare-calatorie
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** asigurari
**Publicat:** 2026-07-25
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-25

**Descriere:** The EHIC is free but does not cover repatriation, private clinics, or trip cancellation. See exactly what each covers, where the gaps are, and when you need both.

**Rezumat rapid:** The European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) is free and gives you access to the public healthcare system in EU countries — but it does NOT cover medical repatriation, private hospitals, mountain rescue, or trip cancellation. For complete protection you need a private travel insurance policy alongside the card. The ideal setup: EHIC for public hospital emergencies in the EU, travel insurance for everything the EHIC does not cover.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: Is the European Health Insurance Card free?**
R: Yes, completely free. It is issued by your national health insurance authority (in Romania, through CNAS at cardeuropean.ro). It is valid for up to 24 months and can be renewed. Apply at least two weeks before departure to ensure you receive it in time.

**Î: Does the EHIC cover medical repatriation?**
R: No, never. The EHIC does not cover repatriation under any circumstances. A medical air ambulance from Western Europe to Romania can cost €15,000–30,000. Without private travel insurance, that cost falls entirely on your family.

**Î: Does the EHIC work at private hospitals?**
R: No. The EHIC only covers providers within the public healthcare system. On ski slopes, most first-aid centres are private — the card does not cover them. In tourist-heavy areas of Greece, Spain, or Italy, many conveniently located clinics are private and the EHIC is not accepted.

**Î: If I have the EHIC, do I still need travel insurance?**
R: Yes, for complete protection. The EHIC covers basic public healthcare in the EU, but not repatriation, private hospitals, mountain rescue, trip cancellation, or lost baggage. Travel insurance covers exactly these gaps — and costs €12–25 for a week in Europe.

**Î: Does the EHIC work outside the EU?**
R: Only within the EU, the European Economic Area (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway), Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. In Turkey, Egypt, the USA, or Asia, the EHIC is not valid — private travel insurance is your only protection.

**Î: Does credit card travel insurance replace a proper policy?**
R: Rarely. Many premium credit cards (Gold, Platinum, Visa Infinite) include travel insurance as a benefit, but with important limitations: typically lower coverage amounts (€10,000–25,000), requirements to have paid the trip with that card, and exclusions for pre-existing conditions. Check your card's terms — it may supplement but usually should not replace a dedicated policy.

**Î: What does travel insurance NOT cover?**
R: Standard exclusions: undeclared pre-existing conditions, accidents under the influence of alcohol or drugs, extreme sports (without a specific add-on), planned medical treatment abroad, travel to conflict zones (MAE level 4 warning), and pandemics (with some insurers). Always read the general conditions before purchasing.

## Best eSIM by Destination 2026: Turkey, USA, Thailand, UK and More

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/esim-roaming/cel-mai-bun-esim-per-destinatie
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** esim-roaming
**Publicat:** 2026-07-25
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-25

**Descriere:** Practical eSIM comparison for the most popular non-EU destinations. Real prices for Airalo, Saily and Yesim, what to avoid, and why you must buy before you leave.

**Rezumat rapid:** For destinations outside the EU, a prepaid eSIM with 5–10 GB costs between €8 and €20 for a week — far cheaper than roaming (€10–15/GB). Airalo, Saily and Yesim are the three most reliable providers. The single most important rule: buy before you leave. In Turkey, the authorities have blocked access to international eSIM provider websites since 2025, making it impossible to purchase once you are in the country.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: How much does an eSIM cost for a week in Turkey?**
R: A 5 GB / 30-day plan for Turkey costs approximately $12 on Airalo. A 10 GB / 30-day plan costs around $18. For typical one-week usage (maps, WhatsApp, social media), 5 GB is enough. The critical requirement: buy before you arrive — Turkish authorities have blocked eSIM provider websites since 2025.

**Î: Does Airalo work in Turkey?**
R: Yes, but with one important condition: you must buy before you arrive. Since 2025, Turkish authorities have blocked access to major eSIM provider websites (including Airalo) for users already in the country. Install the eSIM at home, and it activates automatically when you land.

**Î: Do I need an eSIM for Greece?**
R: No. Greece is in the EU, and EU roaming rules apply — your Romanian mobile plan works in Greece at no extra charge (subject to fair use limits). You only need an eSIM for non-EU destinations like Turkey, UK, USA, Thailand, or Egypt.

**Î: Do I need an eSIM for the UK after Brexit?**
R: Yes. Since Brexit, the UK is no longer part of EU roaming, so your Romanian operator will charge non-EU rates — typically €3–7/day. A UK eSIM (5 GB / 15 days, ~$10–15 on Airalo) is much cheaper than roaming charges.

**Î: How much data do I need in the USA for a week?**
R: For typical use (maps, Uber, WhatsApp, social media, no streaming): 5–8 GB covers a week comfortably. If you use TikTok, Instagram Reels, or Netflix heavily, go for 10–15 GB. Note that US apps often autoplay videos — enable 'Data Saver' mode to reduce consumption.

**Î: Are regional eSIM plans (e.g. 'Europe', 'Asia') cheaper?**
R: Usually not per GB — regional plans are slightly more expensive per gigabyte than country-specific ones. But they are convenient if you are visiting 3+ countries on one trip (e.g. Thailand + Vietnam + Cambodia). For a single destination, the local plan is almost always cheaper.

**Î: Can I use an eSIM and keep my regular SIM card?**
R: Yes — that is exactly the point. Your phone has dual SIM capability: keep your Romanian physical SIM for calls and bank SMS codes, and use the eSIM for data. You activate the eSIM's data connection at the destination, and switch back to your Romanian SIM for calls.

## 10 Cheapest Destinations from Bucharest 2026: Direct Flights Under €100 Return

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/zboruri/cheapest-destinations-from-bucharest
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** zboruri
**Publicat:** 2026-07-31
**Actualizat:** 2026-07-31

**Descriere:** The best-value European city breaks reachable by direct budget flight from Bucharest Henri Coandă Airport in 2026. Real prices, daily budgets, what to see, and when to book for each destination.

**Rezumat rapid:** The cheapest destinations reachable by direct flight from Bucharest in 2026 are: Budapest (from €30 return, 1h20), Rome (from €40, 2h30), Bari (from €40, 2h), Milan (from €45, 2h40), Vienna (from €45, 2h10), Athens (from €50, 2h20), London (from €50, 3h30), Istanbul (from €55, 2h), Barcelona (from €55, 3h10), and Paris (from €60, 3h10). The strategy: book Wizz Air or Ryanair 6–8 weeks ahead, on Tuesday, for mid-week departure. All prices are round-trip per person, achievable outside peak season.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: What is the cheapest destination from Bucharest by plane?**
R: Budapest consistently ranks as the cheapest: Wizz Air flies direct in 1h20 from €30 return. Rome and Bari are close behind (from €40 return). The key to these prices is booking 6–8 weeks ahead, Tuesday–Thursday departures, and avoiding July–August school holiday peak.

**Î: Which airline has the most direct routes from Bucharest?**
R: Wizz Air operates the most routes from Bucharest Henri Coandă (OTP), with 60+ direct destinations across Europe and the Middle East. Ryanair has significantly expanded from Bucharest since 2023 and now offers 35+ direct routes, often competing directly with Wizz Air on price. Tarom serves Western European capitals but at higher prices. Blue Air went bankrupt in 2022 — any Blue Air route is now served by Wizz or Ryanair.

**Î: When are the cheapest flights from Bucharest?**
R: January–March and November offer the lowest prices (avoiding Christmas/New Year). Best value with good weather: May–June and September–October. Peak prices: July–August and school holiday weeks (Easter, 1 May, Christmas). Book Tuesday or Wednesday mornings 6–8 weeks before departure for the best combination of price and availability.

**Î: Do I need a travel visa for these destinations?**
R: No. All 10 destinations in this guide are accessible to Romanian citizens (EU nationals) without a visa. The UK now requires an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA, £10, takes 10 minutes) — apply online at least 72 hours before flying. Turkey requires no visa for stays under 90 days. All other destinations are standard EU freedom of movement.

**Î: Do I need travel insurance for European city breaks?**
R: The European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) covers medical emergencies at public hospitals within the EU — but not repatriation, trip cancellation, lost luggage, or non-EU destinations (UK, Turkey). For UK and Turkey in particular, travel insurance is essential. A week's policy covering Europe costs €12–25 — less than a restaurant dinner.

**Î: Do I need an eSIM for these destinations?**
R: For EU destinations (Rome, Vienna, Budapest, Athens, Barcelona, Paris, Bari, Milan), your Romanian SIM has free EU roaming — no eSIM needed unless your data plan has low limits. For the UK (post-Brexit) and Turkey, your Romanian carrier charges €3–12/day roaming. An eSIM from Airalo costs €5–12 for 7 days and saves €16–70 per trip. Buy before departure — especially for Turkey, where eSIM provider sites are blocked from within the country.

**Î: Which is better — Wizz Air or Ryanair from Bucharest?**
R: Depends on the route. Compare both every time — they don't show each other's prices. Wizz Air is typically cheaper on Eastern European routes (Budapest, Warsaw, Vilnius) and has more direct routes overall. Ryanair often undercuts on Western routes (London Stansted, Barcelona, Madrid, Lisbon) since their Bucharest expansion. Always use a flight comparison tool to see both simultaneously.

**Î: How much does a 3-night city break from Bucharest cost in total?**
R: Budget breakdown for a typical 3-night city break from Bucharest: Flights return: €40–100. Accommodation (3 nights, mid-range hotel): €90–200. Local transport (3 days): €10–30. Food and drink: €60–150. Attractions: €0–60. Total realistic range: €200–540 per person. Budapest, Bari, and Athens offer the best value at the lower end; London and Paris sit at the higher end.

## 10 Cheapest European Destinations Actually Worth Visiting in 2026

**URL:** https://plecari.com/en/city-breaks/cheapest-european-destinations-2026
**Limbă:** English
**Verticală:** city-breaks
**Publicat:** 2026-07-13

**Traducere a:** [destinatii-ieftine-europa-2026](https://plecari.com/ro/city-breaks/destinatii-ieftine-europa-2026)

**Descriere:** The best budget destinations in Europe for 2026, ranked by real daily costs. From Sarajevo to Lisbon, with prices, tips, and what makes each one special.

**Rezumat rapid:** The cheapest European destinations worth visiting in 2026 are: Sarajevo (€45/day), Bucharest (€48/day), Belgrade (€50/day), Kraków (€52/day), Budapest (€55/day), Sofia (€55/day), Porto (€62/day), Tirana (€48/day), Split (€58/day), and Athens (€60/day). These budgets include hostel or budget hotel, three meals, local transport, and 1-2 attractions per day. Eastern Europe and the Balkans offer the best value, but even Western European cities like Porto and Athens are surprisingly affordable.

**Întrebări frecvente:**

**Î: What is the cheapest country in Europe to visit?**
R: Bosnia & Herzegovina, Albania, and North Macedonia are consistently the cheapest countries in Europe for travellers in 2026. A comfortable day in Sarajevo costs around €45, and Tirana around €48 — including a private room, three meals, and activities. Romania, Bulgaria, Serbia, and Poland are close behind at €48-55/day.

**Î: Is Eastern Europe safe for tourists?**
R: Yes. Eastern European cities like Bucharest, Budapest, Kraków, and Belgrade are generally as safe as Western European capitals, with lower rates of tourist-targeting crime than Barcelona or Paris. Standard precautions apply everywhere: use ride-hailing apps, watch for pickpockets in crowded areas, and stick to well-lit streets at night.

**Î: When is the cheapest time to visit Europe?**
R: January-March and November (excluding Christmas/New Year) offer the lowest flight and accommodation prices. For good weather AND reasonable prices, May-June and September-October are the sweet spot — warm enough for outdoor sightseeing, without July-August peak pricing and crowds.

**Î: Can you travel Europe on €50 a day?**
R: In Eastern Europe and the Balkans, €50/day covers a private room in a budget hotel, three meals at local restaurants, public transport, and 1-2 paid attractions. In Western Europe, €50/day requires a dorm bed, self-catering for some meals, and focusing on free attractions. It's tight but doable in cities like Porto, Lisbon, and Athens.
